title: TypeScript Compiler API: Preserving Child Node Narrowing in Reusable Type Guards 🔧
why_read: A focused, technically precise walkthrough of a real TypeScript type-narrowing limitation and how to work around it in reusable type guards.
analysis: This article digs into a specific and genuinely tricky TypeScript problem: how to write a reusable type guard function that preserves not just the top-level narrowed type but also a narrowed property on a nested child object. The author shows that this issue isn't unique to the TypeScript Compiler API's AST types but is a general problem with how TypeScript handles 'property refinement' across function boundaries. This is a legitimate pain point for library authors building type-safe utilities, and understanding it helps engineers write more robust, reusable type-checking code. The explanation is grounded in concrete code examples, making it practically useful rather than abstract.
